data.narrative:
Fulfil is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Mir Aamir that has raised $127M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of three same-stage, same-sector comparables (Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity), supplemented by a broader universe of eight private robotics firms and one public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses total capital raised as a proxy base ($127M) and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage step-ups, yielding $241M. The peer-median method directly references the three same-stage robotics comparables, which show valuations of $1.6B, $1.8B, and $2.0B, with a median of $1.8B. These methods produce materially different signals, reflecting uncertainty around Fulfil's relative positioning within the frontier robotics space.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $205M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $996M. The wide band reflects a fundamental tension: stage-progression mechanics suggest modest valuation relative to capital deployed, while peer-median benchmarking—anchored to well-funded frontier robotics competitors—points substantially higher. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the selected peer set as true comparables and whether the stage-progression multiple adequately captures sector-specific growth dynamics and burn characteristics in capital-intensive robotics ventures.
